strategy.summary: Reproduce jnp.polyfit returning a single (n,n,1) covariance matrix for multi-rhs y with cov=True and full=False. The project's testPolyfit, extended with num_rhs=[1,5], should fail on buggy commit 437d7d88b992 (shape/value mismatch vs numpy.polyfit for num_rhs=5) and pass on the fixed PR #24074 revision. Environment is unbounded for jax/jaxlib (chosen: build from source at the repo revision), numpy constrained only by era (<=2.2), XLA CPU backend.

build_commands: pip install -e . (or build jaxlib via build/build.py for CPU and install the resulting wheel matching the repo revision)
git checkout PR #24074 fixed revision (parent of merge or merge commit) and rebuild/reinstall for the fixed run
pinned_because: numpy <=2.2: era ceiling from PR date 2025-04-22 (era-inferred, not a documented constraint; relied on for numpy version choice)

jax and jaxlib: no documented constraint and no era entry; chosen to build from the same repository revision as the test rather than the reporter's 0.4.34.dev / 0.4.33 versions, so the test and library stay in sync

strategy.reproducing_test: tests/lax_numpy_test.py::LaxBackedNumpyTests::testPolyfit with num_rhs=5 parameter (the sample_product case where shape is one-dimensional and num_rhs=5, cov=True, full=False)
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy 437d7d88b992, testPolyfit cases with num_rhs=5 and cov in {True, 'unscaled'} fail (covariance shape is (n,n,1) instead of (n,n,5), or values scaled by the first residual only, mismatching numpy.polyfit beyond tol_spec). On the fixed PR #24074 revision the same cases pass, with num_rhs=1 cases passing on both revisions.
strategy.numerical_probe: x = np.arange(10).astype(np.float32); np.random.seed(1); y = np.random.rand(10, 3).astype(np.float32); compare jnp.polyfit(x, y, deg=1, cov=True, full=False)[1].shape against numpy.polyfit(x, y, deg=1, cov=True)[1].shape, expecting (2,2,3) and buggy output (2,2,1)

input_output_examples.input: jnp.polyfit(x, y, deg=1, cov=True, full=False) with x=np.arange(10) float32, np.random.seed(1), y shape (10,3)
input_output_examples.expected_output: C shape (2, 2, 3) matching numpy.polyfit, e.g. first rhs [[0.01583048, ...],[-0.07123718, ...]]

risks: The bug appears only when cov is requested with multiple rhs; if the test harness uses an installed wheel rather than the repository source, the test will not exercise the change, so run with the repo on sys.path.

Float32 differences in the trailing digits are within tolerance; the transition relies on the shape/broadcast failure, not on tiny numeric differences, so a value-only comparison at 1e-3 may pass on buggy code for the first rhs.
The test uses jax.default_matmul_precision('float32'); on non-CPU backends or with different default precision the numerical outcome may differ, though the shape mismatch is backend-independent.
The reproduction is confirmed only on XLA CPU as reported; no GPU/TPU behaviour is evidenced, and no sanitiser or specific architecture is required.
The numpy version era constraint (<=2.2) is era-inferred, not documented; a numpy 2.x newer than the PR date could change np.polyfit reference behaviour.
Building jaxlib from source requires a working C++ toolchain and Bazel; if unavailable, the nightly wheel matching the revision date may be used instead, which weakens version pinning.
The fix's intermediate version broke broadcasting/rank promotion, so the fixed-revision pass depends on the final PR state, not an intermediate commit.

oracle.why: Test compares JAX polyfit against numpy.polyfit per rhs with the stated tolerances, and the shape mismatch is an exact check.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 437d7d88b992 the covariance output has shape (n,n,1) for num_rhs=5, while numpy returns (n,n,5); the shape/values comparison fails the assertion because only the first rhs residual scaled the covariance.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the covariance is broadcast per rhs as Vbase[:,:,np.newaxis]*fac[np.newaxis,np.newaxis,:], matching numpy's shape and values within tol_spec, so the assertion passes.
